title: On Windows, a live control child's closed stdout surfaces as a deadline, not end-of-file
outcome: We know why, on Windows, the parent never sees end-of-file when an owned child closes its stdout and stays alive, and the control transport reports that case accurately or the limit is documented.
acceptance: The cause is found from evidence, naming which handle keeps the pipe open and in which process, or the item records what was checked and why it can't be found.

If the cause is in TermAl, a reviewed and gated fix makes a Windows live-child stdout close report end-of-file through the real transport, shown by an actual-child test. Otherwise the limitation is stated in the relevant feature doc.
